title: Named constants conceal k_ and use muted amber
summary: The frontend hides a source k_ prefix and colors the visible constant name in restrained yellow-orange, while retaining double-colon constexpr syntax and exact source reveal.
details: A source identifier such as k_max_int displays as max_int wherever the C/C++/CUDA frontend owns presentation; source-buffer bytes are unchanged.
The renderer classifies the original k_ identifier before stripping its prefix, then applies DansConstant to the visible tail using muted amber #d6a35f without bold emphasis.
Recognized unprefixed constexpr declaration names receive the same constant color without any text change.
Prefix concealment applies to declarations, raw use sites, overlay expressions, array dimensions, and non-type template arguments, and alignment widths are measured after removal.
Strings, comments, includes, and gray static_assert contexts remain protected; cursor and Visual reveal show the exact C++ source spelling, including k_.

The double-colon constexpr auto choice from DEC-019 remains selected, and the double-colon, colon-equals, and visible-auto alternatives remain validated buffer-local profiles; the selected style-lab catalog hash is 39e6f0aec27c93a2f1e3d4e9ad9fc5d176716c8bf8eb66eee437f7408cdfef9a.
rationale: Once a dedicated color conveys constant identity, displaying the naming prefix is redundant and adds visual noise.
A muted yellow-orange is warm enough to distinguish constants without competing aggressively with errors, strings, or brighter library categories.
Classifying before conceal preserves semantic styling at both declaration and use sites without relying on LSP semantic-token coloring.
alternatives: Keep the k_ prefix visible in compile-time purple; superseded because the owner clarified that remove means hide and requested a restrained yellow-orange.
Hide k_ without a distinct semantic color; rejected because constant identity would disappear with the prefix.
Use a bright gold or saturated orange; rejected because it would be too visually aggressive.

Embedded Neovim ext_linegrid captures validate all three constexpr profiles, concealed prefixes, unchanged controls and source, and the selected amber RGB run.
